A bheil sibh ag obair air ùr-ghnàthachadh a tha a’ tighinn am bàrr a dh’fhaodadh bathar, seirbheis no pròiseas ùr no leasaichte a thoirt gu buil? A bheil sibh airson a bhith a’ co-obrachadh le Oilthigh Heriot-Watt, Oilthigh na Gàidhealtachd agus nan Eilean no Oilthigh Raibeart Ghòrdain gus ur cuid ùr-ghnàthachaidh adhartachadh? Ma fhreagair sibh "tha" do na ceistean gu h-àrd, dh’fhaodadh pròiseact Ùr-ghnàthachaidh agus Comas Malairteach TalEntEd ur cuideachadh le bhith a’ toirt seachad taic acadaimigeach, ionmhasail agus leasachaidh gnìomhachais gus an gabh an t-ùr-ghnàthachadh agaibh ceum a dh’ionnsaigh soirbheas. Na tha ri fhaighinn Prògram taic aonaichte a tha a’ gabhail a-steach: • Duaisean maoineachaidh ùr-ghnàthachaidh de £5,000 no £25,000 • Co-obrachadh le prìomh acadaimigich • Taic fhiosraichte bho Mhanaidsear Leasachaidh Ùr-ghnàthachaidh • Ceanglaichean air feadh eag-shiostam ùr-ghnàthachaidh na h-Alba Tha am pròiseact ùr-ghnàthachaidh is comas malairt seo mar phàirt de phrògram TalEntEd Islands le taic bho Aonta Fàs nan Eilean, a tha air a mhaoineachadh le Riaghaltasan na h-Alba agus na RA. Tha prògram TalEntEd Islands ag aonachadh obair Heriot-Watt air a’ phròiseact seo leis an obair aig dà phrìomh oilthigh eile air feadh Arcaibh, Sealtainn agus na h-Eileanan Siar: Oilthigh na Gàidhealtachd agus nan Eilean, a tha a’ stiùireadh leasachadh ionnsachadh san àite-obrach, agus Oilthigh Raibeart Ghòrdain, a tha a’ stiùireadh fàs air sgilean iomairt. Co-obrachadh Acadaimigeach Tha an tabhartas maoineachaidh pròiseict a’ toirt pàirt-thaic do cho-obrachadh le acadaimigeach bho co-dhiù aon de na h-oilthighean a tha ag obair còmhla ann an TalEntEd (Oilthigh Heriot-Watt, Oilthigh na Gàidhealtachd is nan Eilean agus Oilthigh Raibeart Ghòrdain). Obraichidh Manaidsear Leasachaidh Ùr-ghnàthachaidh a’ phròiseict còmhla ri tagraichean gus acadaimigeach a chomharrachadh bho fhear de na trì oilthighean seo a tha a’ dol gu math le ùr-ghnàthachadh ùr agus cuiridh iad còmhraidhean co-obrachail mun phròiseact air dòigh. Maoineachadh pròiseict Tha taic ionmhais a’ phròiseict air a thoirt seachad an dàrna cuid tro thabhartas ùr-ghnàthachaidh de £5k (‘Leasaich’) no £25k (‘Cuir an gnìomh’). Ged a tha raon farsaing de phròiseactan ion-roghnach ann, mar as trice bidh duaisean ‘Leasaich’ a’ toirt taic do sgrùdaidhean sgòpaidh tràth, measadh comasachd agus dealbhadh gnìomhachais tùsail. Cumaidh tabhartasan ùr-ghnàthachaidh taic ri cosgaisean pròiseict taobh a-staigh gnìomhachais no buidheann san treas roinn, ach a-mhàin cosgaisean luchd-obrach no cosgaisean rianachd, a bhios air am meas mar thabhartasan neo-ionmhasail. Taobh a-staigh nan oilthighean a tha a’ co-obrachadh air a’ phròiseact seo, thèid cosgaisean dìreach a’ phròiseict agus an luchd-obrach a phàigheadh, ach chan eil cosgaisean rianachd ion-roghnach agus thèid an làimhseachadh mar thabhartas neo-ionmhasail. They will usually have a maximum term of 3 months. ‘Adopt’ awards, which could be a follow-on from a ‘Develop’ award, will typically have a duration of 6 months. These will tend to focus on early-stage pilot or prototypes, designed to demonstrate value and potentially provide the basis for further investment. Within one of the collaborating universities, direct project and staff costs will be met, with overhead being ineligible and treated as an in-kind contribution. Toggle breadcrumbs menu About Our Policies Complaints Complaints The University is committed to providing an excellent educational experience and high-quality services for our students and service users of the University. Anyone who receives, requests or is directly affected by the services of the University can make a complaint to us. Complaints Handling Procedure We have a duty to provide an effective system for handling complaints and our Complaints Handling Procedure (CHP) allows complainants to raise matters of concern without fear of being disadvantaged or victimised and in the knowledge that their privacy and confidentiality will be respected. Our CHP reflects the University's commitment to valuing complaints and using information from them to help us improve our services. It seeks to resolve dissatisfaction as close as possible to the point of service delivery and to conduct thorough, impartial and fair investigations of complaints so that, where appropriate, we can make evidence-based decisions on the facts of the case. The CHP has two internal stages and a final external stage with the Scottish Public Services Ombudsman (SPSO) , the governing body for complaints in Scotland. We expect the majority of complaints will be handled at Stage 1. If the complainant remains dissatisfied after Stage 1, they can request that we look at it again, at Stage 2. However, if the original complaint is complex or requires an investigation, we will usually consider that complaint as a Stage 2 matter straight away. The Complaints Handling Procedure consists of six parts: Part 1: Introduction and overview Part 2: When to use the CHP : guidance on identifying what is and what is not a complaint, handling complex or unusual complaint circumstances, and what to do if the CHP does not apply. Part 3: The complaints handling process : guidance on handling a complaint through Stages 1 and 2, and dealing with post-closure contact. Part 4: Governance : staff roles and responsibilities and guidance on recording, reporting, publicising and learning from complaints. Part 5: Guide for students and members of the public : information for students and members of the public on how we handle complaints. Unacceptable Actions Procedures : how we will manage unacceptable or unreasonable behaviour. Complaints forms Whilst complaints can be raised in person, by phone and in writing/electronically, we strongly recommend completing the University complaints form which will help to ensure that all aspects of a complaint, including the outcome being sought, are clearly understood by the University. The forms are available below. Stage 1 complaints form : For a straightforward complaint and where it is envisaged that quick resolution can be achieved. Stage 2 complaints form : For a complaint that is complex and likely to require investigation before a resolution can be achieved. Complaints, and any comments on our procedures, should be sent to: complaints@hw.ac.uk Students, staff and other parties may raise with the Quality Assurance Agency Scotland a concern about the University’s management of academic standards or the quality of learning opportunities or about information made available about our provision.
